### chf — Condition Handling Facility (LIB$SIGNAL/ESTABLISH, SYS$UNWIND, SYS$SETEXV)
<sub>scope: in · tier 1 · plan: vms-2e72 · ref: OpenVMS Programming Concepts Manual — Condition Handling; OpenVMS Calling Standard (Condition Handling / Exception Vectors); OpenVMS RTL LIB$ Manual · reviewed 2026-09-14</sub>

Real 4-stage condition dispatch (design-chf-condition-handling.md, rungs 1-5): dispatch_condition() searches the PRIMARY software exception vector, then the LIB$ESTABLISH frame-handler chain, then the SECONDARY and LAST-CHANCE vectors, in the authentic order (lib_signal.c). LIB$ESTABLISH/REVERT/SIGNAL/STOP/ SIG_TO_RET (5 of ~8 core LIB$ CHF entry points) are implemented; the chain is thread-local single-mode userspace (documented, not a per-process fake of a shared facility). SYS$UNWIND is a real frame transfer (rung-2, vms-8802): honors newpc, abandons intervening frames via setjmp/longjmp into an armed VMS$UNWIND_ANCHOR, and on an anchorless ancestor reconstructs the frame by walking the genuine Alpha call chain (PDSC+RSA) through the LIB$GET_*_INVO primitives (rung-3, vms-1fa). SYS$SETEXV establishes the primary/secondary/ last-chance vectors (rung-1, vms-2e72). Hardware faults are bridged to conditions through the SAME dispatcher: SS$_HPARITH from SIGFPE (arith bridge, vms-db3) and SS$_ACCVIO from SIGSEGV/SIGBUS/SIGILL (rung-4, vms-cc8), both Alpha. SYS$DCLEXH registers a real PCB exit handler run LIFO by SYS$EXIT. chf$mech_array frame+depth+savr0 are real; only savr1 stays 0 (host C ABI exposes no VAX/Alpha R1). LIB$SIG_TO_STOP, LIB$MATCH_COND and SYS$EXIV remain absent. Not oracle-verified (local corpus self-tests only, tests/corpus/ tier1-examples/lib_establish.c / lib_sig_to.c / sys_unwind.c) -> implemented, not verified.

### rms-api — RMS programmatic API — entry points, control blocks, file organizations
<sub>scope: in · tier 1 · plan: vms-801 · ref: OpenVMS Record Management Services Reference Manual · reviewed 2026-09-14</sub>

Record Management Services entry points, FAB/RAB/NAM/XAB control blocks, and the three file organizations. On the executive-present path every $OPEN/$CREATE/$ERASE drives the Files-11 ODS-2 ACP ($ASSIGN + IO$_ACCESS/IO$_CREATE/IO$_DELETE), with the pre-flip POSIX open()/creat() body kept only as the honest executive-absent fallback (rms_acp_absent -> rms_posix_*, vms-5f0). Sequential and Relative are real end to end. Cross-process locking, formerly the facility-wide gap (vms-407), is now real on the ACP path: file-level share arbitration (vms-50e) and per-record locking (vms-0dd) both run through the executive DLM ($ENQ/$DEQ, RMS$_RLK on conflict). Indexed (ISAM) is multi-key over the ACP path: alternate keys are authored from the XABKEY chain and read by key-of-reference via SIDR descent (honest narrower gap: index key compression is rejected fail-honest, RMS$_PLG). The stdio CRTL veneer (fopen/fread/fwrite) is a thin binding over these same $ entry points, not raw POSIX (vms-47e/126/3c1). (Non-ACP/ POSIX-defer handles hold no lock, honestly documented.)

### sys-logicalnames — SYS$ Logical-Name Services
<sub>scope: in · tier 1 · plan: vms-d37 · ref: OpenVMS System Services Reference Manual — SYS$CRELNM, SYS$DELLNM, SYS$TRNLNM · reviewed 2026-09-14</sub>

The 3 SYS$ logical-name entry points (CRELNM/DELLNM/TRNLNM) are all implemented. LNM$SYSTEM is executive-resident: create/delete/translate go through /dev/vms (vms_kif_lnm_define/_delete/_translate) so a name defined in LNM$SYSTEM by one process is visible to every other process on the node, with no per-process fallback if the executive is absent (fails honestly with SS$_NOSUCHDEV, per Rule 9/INV-6). LNM$PROCESS/JOB/GROUP tables remain process-private in a local logical_table[] array; JOB/GROUP executive residency (making them visible across the processes of a job/group, as on real VMS) is the deferred half of vms-d37.

### sys-process — SYS$ Process Control
<sub>scope: in · tier 1 · plan: vms-801 · ref: OpenVMS System Services Reference Manual — Process Control Services · reviewed 2026-09-14</sub>

VMS ships ~25 process-control services; OVMX declares 14 (all in sys_process.c now — the routines moved out of sys_misc.c). CREPRC/DELPRC/HIBER/EXIT are real and executive-backed: $CREPRC genuinely fork()+execve()s and registers the child in the executive process table with inherited identity, handing back the executive-assigned VMS PID; $DELPRC resolves its target through the executive (by prcnam within the caller's UIC group, or by VMS PID) before terminating. WAKE routes through the executive (vms_kif_wake) by PID or self. FORCEX/SUSPND/ RESUME now resolve their target through the executive the same way DELPRC does (by prcnam or VMS PID, or self when none), authorize a cross-process signal by GROUP/WORLD, and deliver the signal to the resolved Linux pid — SS$_NONEXPR for a process the executive does not carry, never a raw kill() on a VMS pid cast as a Linux pid (vms-904). WAKE still does not resolve prcnam-by-name (documented gap). SETPRI now resolves its target through the executive the same way DELPRC does (by prcnam or VMS PID, or self when none), authorizes GROUP/WORLD, and applies the priority to the resolved Linux pid -- SS$_NONEXPR for an absent target, never a silent change of the CALLER's own priority for any target (vms-dff7). SYS$CANCEL is a literal no-op returning SS$_NORMAL (facade-risk). SYS$SETPRN and SYS$PROCESS_SCAN are absent.

### sys-security — SYS$ Security Services ($SETPRV/$CHKPRO/$CHECK_ACCESS)
<sub>scope: in · tier 1 · plan: vms-801 · ref: OpenVMS System Services Reference Manual — Security Services · reviewed 2026-09-14</sub>

SYS$SETPRV is now executive-authoritative (vms-pv1): the mask change routes through /dev/vms (vms_kif_setprv), which authorizes the request against this process's permanent/authorized mask — a caller reaching outside it gets the authorized subset with SS$_NOTALLPRIV and cannot widen the authorized mask (SS$_NOPRIV) — and owns the resulting state; if /dev/vms is unreachable it fails honestly (no per-process fake grant, INV-6). The PCB is now a cache of executive-owned state, not the authority. SYS$CHKPRO is implemented with correct SOGW protection-check logic but advisory because zero OVMX callers currently invoke it. SYS$CHECK_ACCESS (a legacy second-opinion access check) was deliberately removed by design (vms-2b8) as a good anti-facade precedent, not a gap to fill. Rights-database and auditing services belong to other facilities (system-management domain).

### dcl-qualifiers — DCL Qualifier Grammar (Engine A / CLD tables)
<sub>scope: in · tier 1 · plan: vms-8ad · ref: OpenVMS Command Definition Utility (CDU) Manual; DCL Dictionary · reviewed 2026-09-14</sub>

Per-verb qualifier validation (Phase 1, vms-097). The parser rejects any qualifier not in a verb's table with the authentic %DCL-W-IVQUAL (or %DCL-W-IVKEYW) BEFORE the handler runs, structurally. Re-censused 2026-09-14 against origin/main: 46 of the 58 builtin verbs carry a validating table (29 real q_* tables + 17 q_none reject-all); 12 verbs remain accept-all (quals == NULL). Since the prior census DEASSIGN and DEFINE gained real q_* tables (DIFFERENCES moved to q_none), so the real-table set is now exactly 29. A real CLI$-callable CDU compiler exists for external images but is not used to generate the builtin tables.

| | Surface | Kind | VMS | Status | Auth | Scope | Evidence / notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ✅ | `dcl-qualifiers$ivqual-enforcement` | feature | Unknown /QUALIFIER on a verb -> %DCL-W-IVQUAL; bad keyword -> %DCL-W-IVKEYW, before the handler runs | verified | real | in | `src/vmsdcl/dcl_parser.c:448` — dcl_validate_qualifiers() (dcl_parser.c:448) is the structural enforcement point; called from dispatch (dcl_exec.c) before every handler. Closes the universal silent-accept hole for the retrofit tranche. |
| 🟡 | `dcl-qualifiers$verb-coverage` | feature | Per-verb qualifier tables validating every DCL verb's /QUALIFIER grammar | partial | real | in | `src/vmsdcl/dcl_builtin.c` — 29 verbs carry a real q_* qualifier table (ANALYZE ASSIGN ATTACH BACKUP CONVERT COPY CREATE DEASSIGN DEFINE DELETE DIRECTORY DUMP INQUIRE LINK MOUNT OPEN PING PRINT PRODUCT PURGE RECALL RENAME REPLY SEARCH SORT SPAWN STOP SUBMIT TYPE); 17 more use q_none (empty table = reject-all, honest over-restriction for verbs whose VMS qualifiers OVMX has not retrofit); 12 remain quals == NULL (accept-all). 46 of 58 validate. |
| ⬜⚠ | `dcl-qualifiers$zero-validation-verbs` | feature | Qualifier validation for the accept-all verbs (SET, SHOW, RUN, MAIL, READ, WRITE, INSTALL, LIBRARY, TCPIP, TELNET, FTP, HELP) | absent | facade-risk | in | `src/vmsdcl/dcl_parser.c:451` — 12 verbs still have quals == NULL in builtin_verbs[]; dcl_validate_qualifiers() returns SS$_NORMAL for them ('not retrofit', dcl_parser.c:451), so any /QUALIFIER is silently accepted rather than rejected with IVQUAL. SET/SHOW mitigate at the sub-verb level (cmd_set_password/accounting/volume run their own shim validators; unknown SET/SHOW keywords still get IVKEYW), and HELP is deliberately accept-all (a /token after HELP is a qualifier TOPIC, vms-01b). The remaining ones are the Phase-1 follow-up (vms-097). |

### dcl-scripting — DCL Scripting / Flow Control ($STATUS, symbols, CALL, ON, DECK)
<sub>scope: in · tier 1 · plan: vms-8ad · ref: OpenVMS DCL Dictionary; OpenVMS User's Guide (command procedures) · reviewed 2026-09-14</sub>

Command-procedure control flow. The four worst honesty gaps are closed: $STATUS is stored/shown VMS-style ("%Xhhhhhhhh") and refreshed on command-not-found on the shared dispatch path (so a typo'd command in a .COM trips IF .NOT.$STATUS); CALL/SUBROUTINE and DECK/EOD are real constructs; and local symbols get a real per-command-level frame. Re-censused 2026-09-14 against origin/main: unchanged in substance; evidence lines re-anchored. F$MODE remains the one narrow gap.

### queues — Queues + Batch/Print (queue manager, SUBMIT/PRINT)
<sub>scope: in · tier 1 · plan: vms-8ad · ref: OpenVMS System Management Utilities Reference Manual — Queue Manager · reviewed 2026-09-14</sub>

### privileges — Privileges (Definition + Enforcement)
<sub>scope: in · plan: vms-8ad · ref: OpenVMS Guide to System Security ch. 3 (Privileges) · reviewed 2026-09-14</sub>

All 39 VMS privilege bits are defined. Mode-transition and SETPRV enforcement in the kernel executive are real and verified — including a bit-position bug (SETPRV mismapped to DETACH) caught and fixed against lab-VAX SDA. ### protection-acl — File Protection (SOGW/UIC) + ACLs
<sub>scope: in · plan: vms-8ad · ref: OpenVMS Guide to System Security ch. 5 (Protecting Data) · reviewed 2026-09-14</sub>

SOGW/UIC protection is kernel-enforced by the Files-11 ACP and VERIFIED against a real /dev/vms over a real-VAX ODS-2 fixture (test_syssvc_acp_access): a genuinely unprivileged non-owner is refused SS$_NOPRIV where a system-group process succeeds — same code, opposite verdict. The Delete bit is not enforced in the ACP check (advisory). $CHKPRO computes correctly but nothing calls it. The legacy $CHECK_ACCESS 2nd-opinion routine was deliberately removed (vms-2b8) rather than left as a facade. ACLs are undefined beyond constants. Privilege overrides (BYPASS/READALL/SYSPRV) are honored in the ACP; GRPPRV is not (cross-ref privileges).

### sysuaf — SYSUAF — Accounts + Login Authentication
<sub>scope: in · plan: vms-8ad · ref: OpenVMS Guide to System Security; Authorize Utility Manual · reviewed 2026-09-14</sub>

Full UAF account record storage and Purdy/hashed password authentication are real. Account-state login enforcement is genuine: DISUSER/DISACNT deny login (console + SSH) and CAPTIVE confines the session — both read at login time (vms-c8fa). SSH performs the executive setident + a permanent, fail-closed UIC credential drop (vms-49e/vms-6ae), closing the old authenticate-then-run-as-root facade. Password expiration is ENFORCED at login on both front-ends (vms-c6df): an expired password (admin-forced UAI$M_PWD_EXPIRED, or UAF$Q_PWD_DATE+UAF$Q_PWD_LIFETIME elapsed) is refused rather than logged straight in; the interactive force-change flow VMS runs in its place is the tracked follow-up (honest-refuse floor, INV-6). A NETWORK-class login authorization decision (DISNETWORK + the account/expiry gates) now exists and is selftest-proven fail-closed, but is deliberately unwired into any live login path pending the SSH->LOGINOUT session-establish (vms-843a/vms-16b).

Permits a network login only if the account is enabled (DISUSER/DISACNT), UAI$M_DISNETWORK is clear, and the password is not expired; grants nothing beyond the SYSUAF record. ### cluster-dlm — Cluster-wide Distributed Lock Manager
<sub>scope: in · plan: vms-694 · ref: OpenVMS Cluster Systems manual; $ENQ/$DEQ/$GETLKI system services · reviewed 2026-09-14</sub>

The ENQ-class distributed lock manager is IMPLEMENTED and executive-resident: all DLM state is real executive state (resource blocks, granted/waiting queues, origin records), no per-process fake ever answers (INV-6), and absence is an honest SS$_UNSUPPORTED. On a real /dev/vms executive the SINGLE-NODE rungs are proven via tests/qemu/test_syssvc_dlm_xnode.c (injected cross-node CSID): the register-after-open handshake (rung 0, vms-4b6); the transport, receive-side grant, block-then-grant queue, and async reply wire (rungs 1-3/H5, vms-94c/e8f1/904c/6ca); and the blocking-AST holder-side receive (H6, vms-76d/#918). The executive-resident SCS DLM arm (src/kernel-core/vms_dlm_scs.c, send + receive legs) has landed, and 2-node LAB CAPTURES exist for the LVB crossing, the LDWV fallback, and the rebuild paths.
NOT YET RE-PROVEN end-to-end (implemented, not verified): the MULTI-NODE rungs -- LVB write/read crossing (H8/H9), dynamic remaster (H10a/b), directory-ownership refusal (e84), and the distributed-deadlock single-victim search (H11). Their original real-/dev/vms QEMU harnesses (run_dlm_harness_h8/_h9/_h10/_h10b/_e84/ _ec75) were RETIRED with the userspace SCSD daemon in the #1052 executive-resident pivot; a GATED multi-node /dev/vms successor through the landed SCS arm is still being re-established (vms-1ee) and there is no multi-node DLM CI leg yet (vms-1da5). The wire byte layout is OVMX-DERIVED, not yet gated against a real-VAX DLM oracle capture (Rule 8; see the scs-transport row). See kernel-executive.yaml for the single-node lock manager this builds on. Further DEPTH beyond the ENQ-class engine: the concurrent-both-initiate deadlock idempotence proof (vms-04f -- global-min selection ships and is code-verified, now exercised by a host FSM proof) and a real app-process cross-node lock ACQUISITION path (vms-d1f, post-1.0 -- an application $ENQ of a remotely-mastered resource still returns the honest SS$_UNSUPPORTED "0.4" stub).

| 🟢 | `cluster-dlm$directory-redirect` | feature | Directory REDIRECT: a cross-node $ENQ that reaches a node which does not master the tree is answered with the master's CSID (Davis p. 6-31 outcome 2), not declined | implemented | real | in | `src/kernel-core/vms_lock.c` — rd vms-b96, retiring the honest interim "verify-and-reject". Before this, an inbound cross-node $ENQ for a tree this node does not master returned SS$_UNSUPPORTED with no further information, so the requester learned nothing and could only re-resolve blind. The engine now ANSWERS it: when the executive holds the tree's master CSID it replies VMS_DLM_STS_REDIRECT with master_csid set to that node — the book's outcome 2 — and the requester's already-shipping redirect handler (vms_dlm_scs_fsm.c h_redirect) re-addresses. IT IS A REPLY, NEVER A FORWARD. That is the termination argument: exactly one node answers, so no chain of nodes can form and no cycle can be entered. Three responder guards close the single hop: no master held -> decline; target is this node -> decline; target is the REQUESTER -> decline (that answer would bounce the request straight back). The requester's own DLM_REQ_MAX_REDIRECTS budget bounds the exchange from the other end. INV-6: the CSID named is read off the resource block at the moment of the answer, and it can only have got there from a GRANT a master really sent or a directory reply the cluster really returned. The DIRECTORY node this node's own weight vector resolved is NEVER named as a master — a directory is not a master, and asserting one as master is the fabrication that made a real VAX install OVMX as the master of resources it did not master. There is no code path by which a caller-supplied value reaches the target (the request's own master_csid input is not read on the ENQ path), and the retired OVMX_DLM_ENQ_CSID env crutch has no residual. HONEST RESIDUAL, not papered: this is the ENGINE's decision and its readback. The cat-0x82 reply codec grounds a GRANT shape and a DENY shape only (vms_cluster_codec_dlm.h) — no grounded field carries another node's CSID — and the master/directory-side wire arm (vms_dlm_scs.h's handle_request) is not implemented in kernel-core yet. So no REDIRECT frame is emitted today, and none is fabricated: until a reply shape is grounded from a capture, what leaves this node is still the decline, which the requester's FSM correctly turns into a bounded re-resolve. The over-the-wire multi-node redirect rides the capture-gated rig with the rest of the retired multi-node DLM proofs (vms-1ee).

### connection-manager — Connection manager / membership / quorum / rejoin
<sub>scope: in · plan: vms-694 · ref: OpenVMS Cluster Systems manual (connection manager, quorum algorithm); VAXcluster Principles ch. 7 (CLUB/CSB) · reviewed 2026-09-10</sub>

The connection manager is EXECUTIVE-RESIDENT (vms_cnxman.c and four pure FSMs in vms.ko / the NetBSD vms.kmod). FC-P3.9 deleted the userspace SCS daemon that previously carried the join, the quorum arithmetic and a membership block it wrote into the executive by ioctl — the operator's 2026-09-02 clustering reset ruled that stack a non-portable strawman. READ THE STATUSES LITERALLY. Verified is the MODEL and the LOCAL machinery (CLUB/CSB, the ten-state ladder, join drive, 12-step barrier, coordinator, reconnect, quorum arithmetic) at R1/R2 with the readback ioctls at R3/R4 — AND, as of the symmetric-CN=2 proof, the DISTRIBUTED outcome for OVMX^n: two real /dev/vms executives form a cluster (one FOUNDS from nothing on quorum by its own votes, the other JOINS and reaches MEMBER), CN=2 read from real executive state on both. The CSID mechanism that gated this is now PINNED on a real-VMS capture (integration note E30, resolved): the coordinator assigns a round-robin, monotonically-advancing CSV slot (NOT sysid&0x3ff), sent per member in a cat-0x01 op-0x05 membership record; the joiner ADOPTS its own assigned CSID, never self-derives. What is STILL NOT verified: (a) a real-VAX mixed cluster — OVMX joining or admitting a genuine OpenVMS node (connection-manager$real-vax-join, absent — this proof is OVMX^n only); (b) the cross-node DLM (the cluster-dlm rows stay implemented until vms-1ee's multi-node /dev/vms proof lands); (c) quorum on a joiner (it counts members but has not yet learned peer VOTES via op-01 PARAMS). Every row below says which it is.

Recomputed on every membership transition from the CLUB's own state: per-node VOTES come from each CSB's advertised PARAMS record and are NOT counted until `params_valid` is set -- an un-advertised VOTES is not an advertised zero. EXPECTED_VOTES is this node's own SYSGEN value. STARTUP.EXE loads the cluster SYSGEN parameters (VMS_IOCTL_SYSGEN_LOAD), then issues VMS_IOCTL_CLUSTER_START, which starts the fork thread, PEA0:, SCS and the connection manager and forms or joins per VAXCLUSTER -- all of it at boot Step 2d, BEFORE run_startup() and every MOUNT that STARTUP.COM drives. That ordering is the point: a cluster that started from a DCL phase would be a different operating system. VAXCLUSTER=0 issues no ioctl at all (no PEA0:, no HELLO, no console line); =2 with nowhere to join prints VMS's own "waiting to form or join an OpenVMS Cluster" and keeps sweeping; =1 reports STANDALONE. The console line is rendered from the executive's OWN cluster state, read back from struct vms_cluster, never composed from the ioctl's status -- so a JOINING node is never announced as a MEMBER. PROVEN AT R1 (test_cnxman_boot.c pins the step ordering and the state rendering; test_cluster_boot_gate.c the VAXCLUSTER gate) and R4 negctl (tests/qemu/test_cluster_start_negctl.sh). ### nisca — NISCA/NISCS LAN transport
<sub>scope: in · plan: vms-694 · ref: OpenVMS Cluster Systems manual; NISCA/NISCS wire protocol (Systems Application A) · reviewed 2026-09-03</sub>

The LAN transport under SCS: genuine raw-Ethernet frames on the LAVC/SCA ethertype, not a UDP/IP tunnel standing in for the real wire. Now the EXECUTIVE's own port driver (PEDRIVER role, PEA0:) rather than a userspace daemon's raw socket — FC-P3.9 deleted that daemon.


<sub>3 items · 3 met · 0 in progress · 0 not started</sub>

| | Surface | Kind | VMS | Status | Auth | Scope | Evidence / notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 🟢 | `nisca$lan-transport` | protocol | NISCA/SCA raw-Ethernet transport, ethertype 0x6007 (LAVC/SCA) | implemented | real | in | `src/kernel-core/vms_pe.c` — FC-P0.9. The datalink is opened IN KERNEL CONTEXT (exec_l2_open(), the exec_kbackend seam: AF_PACKET on Linux, the NetBSD equivalent on the vax substrate), so a booted node needs no CAP_NET_RAW anywhere in userspace -- there is no userspace raw socket on the cluster path at all any more. Real frames on 0x6007, never a UDP/IP tunnel. The HELLO multicast address is derived from the cluster group number as real VMS does it -- AB-00-04-01-<LE16(group + 0x100)>, the mapping VMS prints for itself at SYSMAN CONFIGURATION SHOW CLUSTER_AUTHORIZATION -- and the SAME derived value is both the transmit destination and the address enabled in the LAN device's multicast filter, so the two cannot diverge (rd vms-147; through V0.7 the derivation omitted the +0x100 and was correct for group 1 only). Grounded on three real-VMS oracles (V7.3/VAX group 1, V5.5-2H4/VAX group 257, V8.4/Alpha group 2026), pinned with refutations in tests/cluster/host/test_codec_hello.c. The group is on the wire a SECOND time, at abs 22..23 of every SCA frame, as a plain LE16(group) -- a different encoding of the same number, not the same arithmetic as the address. Both are read from the ONE CLUSTER_AUTHORIZE record in pe_build_identity(), so they cannot diverge (rd vms-b34; through V0.7 abs 22 was the constant 0x0001, right for group 1 only -- a real group-257 OpenVMS VAX V7.3 member discarded every VC STACK OVMX sent it and the circuit never opened). Four oracles (V7.3/VAX group 1, V7.3/VAX group 257, V5.5-2H4/VAX group 257, V8.4/Alpha group 2026), pinned with refutations in the same test; the port's emit/refuse behaviour in tests/cluster/host/test_pe_group_on_wire.c. A frame carrying another cluster's group is refused and counted, never processed. PROVEN AT R1/R2/R3, in CI: tests/cluster/host/test_pe_*.c (the pure port FSM: channels, HELLO cadence, circuit formation, TIMVCFAIL, sequence/ack); the N-node simulator's virtual LAN; tests/qemu/test_cluster_vc.sh drives CLUSTER_DIAG_PORT against a real /dev/vms on a booted node. NOT claimed: interoperation with a real VAX's PEDRIVER on a live LAN -- that is R5, LAB-DEFERRED.
 |
| 🟢 | `nisca$discovery-revisions` | protocol | NISCA discovery HELLO — both observed on-wire revisions | implemented | real | in | `src/kernel-core/vms_cluster_codec_hello.c` — rd vms-0f8. OVMX's discovery corpus was harvested entirely from OpenVMS VAX V7.3 nodes (message class 0x05, 120-byte SCA content). A real OpenVMS VAX V5.5-2H4 node speaks a SECOND revision of the same HELLO: class 0x03, 114-byte content, no abs 128-133 tail, and two differing marker words at abs 94/126 -- and NOTHING else different, field position for field position, across 53 captured frames in which the only span that moves is the live tick at abs 96 (docs/cluster-protocol-spec.md 4(b.c3)). (This entry once counted abs 22 as a third marker; it is the CLUSTER GROUP number, LE16 -- the two specimens compared came from clusters 1 and 257 -- corrected under rd vms-b34, which also stopped the port echoing a peer's group back at it.) Through V0.7 the executive classified every such frame family 0/UNCLASSIFIED and counted it badclass. The codec now carries both revisions as a TABLE, keyed on the class byte AND the exact content length, so a class-0x03 frame at any other length stays UNKNOWN and is counted rather than guessed at. The port LEARNS which revision a peer speaks off that peer's own frame -- per channel for directed frames, port-wide first-wins for the multicast advertisement -- the same on-wire-assignment discipline already used for the cluster join nonce and the abs 47-67 discovery-format span, never a version table compiled in. No meaning is claimed for the differing marker values; they are carried as data exactly as the 0x05 revision's already are, and every field that asserts something about THIS node (SCSNODE, SCSSYSTEMID, hardware MAC, incarnation, tick) stays this node's own and is never echoed. PROVEN AT R1 (CI) AND R5 (live, against a REAL OpenVMS VAX V5.5-2H4): the browser-demo capture tests/lab/captures/vms-0f8-browser-c03-channel-20260923/ shows Node C->OVMX badclass fall from 553-of-553 to 402-of-1838 -- and every residual is ONE non-discovery shape (that node's SCS envelope, format byte 0x03, a SEPARATE second revision, NOT decoded). The sec 4(a).1 channel opened bidirectionally in this revision: one b2 from the member, 186 b3 from OVMX, 184 b4 CONFIRMs back, and OVMX's reply carries the cluster join nonce it LEARNED off that member's own b2 (77 11 7a 7d), its own SCSNODE/SCSSYSTEMID/MAC, and the peer's revision markers. In CI: tests/cluster/host/test_codec_hello.c (classification, parse, byte-exact round trip of the real specimen, and the refusals) and tests/cluster/host/test_pe_rev_c3.c (the real 128 bytes through pe_fsm_rx: badclass 0, peer identity off the wire, the reply emitted in the peer's revision carrying our own identity, plus 257 truncations and bit-flips that must not fault). Specimen provenance: the multicast hello-c3-vaxc-v55.spec and the DIRECTED b2 hello-c3-vaxc-directed-b2.spec under tests/cluster/host/fixtures/, both origin `capture`, both hashed in docs/clean-room/reference-captures.sha256. NOT claimed, and the reason CN=2 does not yet form: this revision's SCS LAYER. The same V5.5 node's SCS envelope carries format byte 0x03 at abs 31 rather than the 4(d) constant 0x13, msgtype 0x01 rather than the 4(g) phase-2 0x41, and a body 16 bytes shorter -- a SEPARATE second revision on which OVMX's whole SCS/CM/DLM stack is keyed, and of which exactly ONE specimen exists (that node's round-0 START, retransmitted because nothing answered it). It is not decoded and this register does not extrapolate it. Nor is a 4(k) padded frame claimed in the discovery revision -- none has ever been observed, so the port DECLINES to probe such a peer and records that it declined, rather than credit a packet size it never proved.
 |
| 🟢 | `nisca$pea0-device` | feature | PEA0: — the LAN cluster port device | implemented | real | in | `src/kernel-core/vms_pe.c` — FC-P0.9/FC-P0.11. The port comes up from the executive at VMS_IOCTL_CLUSTER_START, gated on the VAXCLUSTER the SYSGEN load actually committed: VAXCLUSTER=0 means NO PEA0: and no HELLO at all (the honest silence INV-6 requires, refused twice over -- at the boot-path gate and again inside vms_pe_start). ### scs — SCS — System Communication Services core
<sub>scope: in · plan: vms-694 · ref: OpenVMS Cluster Systems manual; Systems Application A (SCS/SCA architecture) · reviewed 2026-09-03</sub>

The SCS message/connection layer OVMX's cluster wire stack is built on. It is now EXECUTIVE-RESIDENT: a table-driven CDT state machine (vms_scs_fsm.c) with its glue in vms_scs.c, inside vms.ko and the NetBSD vms.kmod. FC-P3.9 deleted the userspace SCS daemon the previous rows described, executing the operator's 2026-09-02 clustering reset. WHAT IS VERIFIED AND WHERE: R1 host unit + R2 N-node simulator + R3 substrate contract, all in CI. R4 (booted OVMX nodes) has legs but they are the cluster harness's, not a graded multi-node run; R5 (a real VAX) is LAB-DEFERRED and nothing here claims it.

A pure [state][event] CDT table (ten frozen states, connect/ accept/reject/disconnect half-exchanges, the credit ledger, the SB path-block CDT queue and the VC-break scan) plus vms_scs.c's glue, which binds it DOWN to the port and registers SCS$DIRECTORY. Every send SPENDS a real credit; SCS never retries and never re-opens a connection on its own. NEVER-CRASH-A-PEER (vms-5339/#1200+#1202), build-enforced: the whole cluster peer-RECEIVE decode surface -- the DLM body decoders + CM PARAMS + the hello/scs/cm/vc/blk frame codecs (24 decoders; MSCP gate-deferred) -- is fuzzed under ASan/UBSan (~3M inputs total) as a CI gate: no over-read / OOB / UB / crash on any malformed, truncated, or hostile peer frame, and each fuzz asserts dispatch-count>0 (non-vacuity) so a silently-never-reached decoder fails the gate rather than shipping a green facade (INV-6). Locks the never-crash-a-peer invariant as a build-time fact, not an aspiration.

An honest, documented partial, not a facade.

### librarian — LIBRARIAN (.OLB Object Libraries + .TLB/.HLB)
<sub>scope: in · plan: vms-59a · ref: OpenVMS LIBRARIAN Utility Reference Manual; VSI OpenVMS DCL Dictionary (LIBRARY) · reviewed 2026-09-14</sub>

LIBRARIAN.EXE now EXISTS and is built + installed to SYS$SYSTEM (was design-only at the last census). It creates/maintains .OLB object libraries — an OVMX-labeled `ar` container of .OBJ (ELF) members (Rule 8: VMS's LBR byte layout is unpublished) — with /CREATE /INSERT /DELETE /LIST /EXTRACT, and LINK.EXE resolves undefined symbols by selectively pulling members. The DCL LIBRARY command drives the same .OLB path plus OVMX text/help libraries (.TLB/.HLB, an OVMX "LBRO" format, Rule 8). Proven end-to-end (build .OLB → link → activate → run) and byte-identical-twice (reproducible archives). LIBRARIAN.EXE now ALSO runs AS an OVMX-native image (like LINK/TCC/DCL): built by mk_librarian.sh (-DOVMX_OLB_RMS_IO) into a PT_INTERP=IMGACT.EXE image, it is IMGACT-activated and /CREATEs an .OLB reading each .OBJ and writing the .OLB through RMS (sys$open/$get, sys$create/$put), proven byte-exact by run_librarian_native.sh — the S3-spine step toward MMK building a component inside OVMX (vms-1df).

### object-format — Object File Format
<sub>scope: in · plan: vms-ade · ref: VSI OpenVMS Linker Utility Manual (object module format); binutils include/vms (public GPL) EVAX record layouts · reviewed 2026-09-14</sub>

LINK.EXE ingests two object inputs. (1) Standard ELF relocatable objects and `ar` whole-archive containers — the OVMX self-host path; the container is OVMX's own (ELF) where VMS's OBJ$ record format is not published at byte level (Rule 8). (2) NEW: native Alpha/VMS "EVAX" object modules produced by the `alpha-dec-vms` GCC/binutils port — the linker reads that intrinsic VMS object format UNCHANGED (records, EGSD psects+symbols, ETIR reloc stack-machine, materialized psect content), so the port keeps its VMS identity rather than being forced to emit ELF. EVAX layouts are clean-room from the public binutils include/vms headers and verified byte-exact against fixtures the reference `alpha-dec-vms-as` emits. VAX OBJ$ records remain out.

### decnet — DECnet Phase IV (Routing, NSP, Task-to-Task, SET HOST)
<sub>scope: in · plan: vms-30e · ref: DECnet for OpenVMS Networking Manual; DNA Phase IV Routing + NSP specs · reviewed 2026-09-14</sub>

No longer greenfield: src/vmsdecnet now carries real, clean-room Phase IV wire codecs and a routing adjacency engine, several oracle-verified byte-identical against captures committed in docs/decnet-provenance-register.md (lab specimens, rd vms-3be/PR #665). Present: the Ethernet Endnode Hello codec (oracle-verified), the Router Hello codec (spec-derived), the routing adjacency state machine + hello/listen timers, and the NSP transport codec (Connect Initiate oracle-verified; other PDUs self-round-trip). A live engine/socket now drives real logical links over the datalink: inbound SET HOST reaches an AUTHENTICATED LOGINOUT (decnet$cterm-session-auth), the outbound DCL SET HOST CLIENT is wired (decnet$set-host), and inbound file COPY / FAL (object 17) authenticates the connect-carried credentials and moves a file through DAP + RMS (decnet$fal / decnet$dap). Still open: general task-to-task ($QIO), and the outbound COPY-over-datalink client wired into a DCL process. NODE"acc"::file filespec syntax parses and DCL COPY now routes it to the FAL path (reporting honestly until the outbound bridge lands). Real-VAX oracle status (rd vms-a70): OUTBOUND SET HOST is now PROVEN live against a real VMS VAX V7.3 -- OVMX's DCL SET HOST client drives a complete DECnet Phase IV CTERM session (CI -> CC -> NSP link-service -> CTERM foundation negotiation -> LOGINOUT -> authenticated DCL -> remote commands with live output -> clean LOGOUT), wire-verified in tests/lab/captures/decnet-sethost-dcl-20260911/ (the session's own _RTA1: process appears in its own SHOW SYSTEM output). The CTERM foundation/Bind protocol was re-grounded byte-for-byte on the real oracle (decnet$sc-connect + the foundation codec), retiring the earlier OVMX-labelled facade. Still open on the DECnet SET HOST bracket: the INBOUND direction (real VAX -> OVMX-as-CTERM-server -> OVMX LOGINOUT) is not yet live-proven (needs the booted OVMX executive; decnet$cterm-session-auth stays partial), plus general task-to-task ($QIO) and the outbound COPY-over-datalink client. 1.0 track (vms-30e).

The daemon holds no credential, spawns nothing, and the carried username reaches no decision; there is no fork/execvp/openpty anywhere above the VMS layer (standing gate tests/integration/test_creprc_session_primitive.sh check 5, both directions + negctl). NOT yet: one session at a time, no CTERM read-solicitation flow (byte-transparent pump), no DCL `SET HOST` client wiring (decnet$set-host), no live-VAX bracket. The authentication proof (challenged, bad credentials REFUSED, $GETDVI RTAn: cross-process) is DECNETD.EXE --cterm-accept-test against the real /dev/vms + real LOGINOUT, run by the shared acceptance battery in the booted image -- it FAILS honestly where the executive is absent (INV-6), it does not degrade to a stub. CTERM FOUNDATION PROTOCOL RE-GROUNDED (rd vms-a70): the CTERM foundation/Bind wire protocol is NO LONGER a facade -- it was re-grounded byte-for-byte on the real oracle (the foundation short-TLV + msgtype-9 envelope codec, host-speaks-first negotiation FSM, NSP link-service credit grant, prompt-gated Read Data) and PROVEN interoperable with a real OpenVMS VAX V7.3 in the OUTBOUND direction: OVMX's SET HOST client drove a full authenticated CTERM session to a live DCL on a real VAX (decnet$set-host, tests/lab/captures/decnet-sethost-dcl-20260911/). ### ssh — SSH remote login
<sub>scope: in · plan: vms-9ef · ref: VSI OpenVMS TCP/IP Services — SSH server (OpenSSH port) · reviewed 2026-09-15</sub>

The SSH SERVER itself is not yet present. The faithful target (rd vms-9ef) is the REAL upstream OpenSSH port compiled NATIVELY on the TCP/IP + OVMX substrate (VMS C-RTL / DECC$SHR, the DECC$SOCKET/$QIO BGn: socket surface, a VMS PTY, and the genuine network-login -> LOGINOUT -> DCL path), shipping inside the TCP/IP Services kit. That port does not yet build, because the substrate it needs is still being built up (rd vms-9ef tree, R1-R4). An earlier hand-rolled stand-in — VMSSSHD.EXE plus a --wrap veneer over an OpenSSH binary and a $CREPRC(LOGINOUT) handoff shim — was RETIRED (rd vms-d916) because it was LARP, not the real port: green-of-a-stand-in counts as nothing (INV-6). What DOES exist and is unit-tested are the substrate seams the real port will bind: the ordered fail-closed credential drop (cred_drop.c) and the fail-honest executive identity (ssh_ident.c) — both already consumed by the TCP/IP inetd per-service run-as drop — plus the OVMX TERM->device mapping (term_map.c), unit-tested but not yet wired into a production caller, and, in the executive, the network-login pre-auth stamp (VMS_IOCTL_TERM_SETLOGIN/GETLOGIN, vms-65b) and the BGn: server socket path (bind/listen/accept over genuine $QIO, vms-698). The capability is reported honestly as not-yet-present rather than as a green facade.

### tcpip-services — TCP/IP Services (UCX QIO + Sockets + BGn:/ETH0:)
<sub>scope: in · plan: vms-67f · ref: OpenVMS TCP/IP Services for OpenVMS (UCX) manuals · reviewed 2026-09-14</sub>

A THIN BUT REAL SLICE of TCP/IP Services, not the product. What EXISTS is real; the majority of the OpenVMS UCX application surface is NOT built and is now tracked as absent rows below (unbuilt-application-surface, sockets-api-gaps). DATA PLANE: a VMS program reaches TCP the ordinary VMS way — $ASSIGN TCPIP$DEVICE: then $QIO on the executive-resident INET pseudo-device BGn: (src/kernel/vms_bg*, socket lives in vms.ko over the host in-kernel socket API, no userspace stack), proven end-to-end against a real /dev/vms and guarded by a negctl defect gate. A BSD-sockets RTL veneer (DECC$SOCKET-equivalent) rides that path, and the client TOOLS (DCL TELNET/FTP + PING), the TCPIP$INETD auxiliary server and a DAYTIME service are real. The NIC now surfaces as the VMS device ETH0: and QEMU provides a virtio-net-pci device (default user-mode NAT). CONFIG PLANE (vms-67f): host name/domain/address land in the executive-resident TCPIP$INET_HOST/DOMAIN/HOSTADDR SYSTEM logicals AND PERSIST ACROSS REBOOT — host/interface/route/name-service settings are written to TCPIP$*.DAT over the Files-11 ACP (apply/persist split) and reapplied at startup (TCPIP REAPPLY), proven by a double-boot e2e. INBOUND is R4-hardened: TCPIP$INETD drops each spawned service to its own SYSUAF run-as account before execv (fail-closed, never SYSTEM — vms-8bd) and caps concurrent service children (MAXCHILD fork-flood back-pressure — vms-bb4). INV-6 honest throughout: no /dev/vms => SS$_NOSUCHDEV, never a per-process fake. The INETD SERVICE database is now MANAGED THE VMS WAY (#878): TCPIP {SET,SHOW,ENABLE,DISABLE,DELETE} SERVICE edit SYS$SYSTEM:TCPIP$SERVICE.DAT and persist the change over the Files-11 ACP, so a DCL-enabled service survives reboot and is reapplied on the next TCPIP$INETD start (was hand-edit-only). Deferred honestly: DHCP, multiple interfaces / TCPIP$INET_HOSTADDRn, and a raw NIC-as-VMS-device data path (EWA0:).

The end-to-end cold-boot double-boot serving proof (a DCL-enabled service answered on the next boot — the 'verified' oracle gate) is the tracked follow-on. |

None of the real UCX servers/daemons above exist. Recorded as an explicit absent row so the register does not read as near-complete -- this is the bulk of the facility, post-1.0. (Baron 2026-09-16 anti-LARP: TCP/IP is a mile wide, inch deep; this row makes the width honest.) |

## H. Executive

_The VMS executive itself — access modes, the process model (PCB), scheduling, and the executive-backed IPC that underpins the system services. (Architecture/platform support and OVMX self-hosting are roadmap concerns, not compatibility surfaces — see the release roadmap and release-dimensions, not this register.)_

`🟢🟢🟢🟢🟢🟢🟢🟢🟢🟢🟢🟢🟢🟢🟢🟢🟡🟡🟡🟡🟡🟠🟠🟠`  —  9 surfaces catalogued (6 met · 2 in progress · 1 not started) · V1: 9 committed, 6 met

### kernel-executive — Kernel Executive (/dev/vms substrate: EF/locks/AST/mailbox/access-modes/PCB)
<sub>scope: in · plan: vms-6b8 · ref: OpenVMS VAX/Alpha Internals and Data Structures (executive primitives underlying the SYS$ layer) · reviewed 2026-08-31</sub>

The kernel-mediated substrate SYS$ system services are built on: event flags, lock manager, ASTs, mailboxes, logical-name store, and access modes are real and kernel-resident behind /dev/vms (vms_kif). Process control (PCB) is partial and honestly advisory: the PCB is executive-resident and shared (not a per-process fake), $WAKE/$HIBER are executive-resident, and $DELPRC resolves its target in the executive under an oracle-grounded WORLD-privilege gate — the terminate itself is a real Linux SIGTERM (OVMX-LOCAL, documented). Scheduling is honestly stubbed — OVMX has no VMS priority scheduler.

## I. Languages & Compilers

_The VMS language story: compilers (Fortran/COBOL/BASIC/Pascal/MACRO/Ada/PL/I/…), their language RTLs (FOR$/COB$/BAS$/PAS$), and the OpenVMS Calling Standard that makes cross-language calls work. OVMX today has one language — C, via tcc._

`🟢🟡🟡🟡🟡🟡⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜⬜`  —  22 surfaces catalogued (1 met · 5 in progress · 16 not started) · V1: 6 committed, 1 met

### calling-standard — OpenVMS Calling Standard
<sub>scope: in · plan: vms-801 · ref: VSI OpenVMS Calling Standard · reviewed 2026-09-14</sub>

The convention that lets any VMS language call any other: argument-list layout, by-ref/by-value/by-descriptor passing, the standard data types, condition handling, and register/stack usage. OVMX implements enough for C on x86_64 and aarch64; the cross-language data-type surface (packed decimal, varying strings, array descriptors, VAX float) is where it thins out — the descriptor CLASS enum is now fully declared in descrip.h, but only classes S/D are marshalled by any RTL.


<sub>4 items · 0 met · 4 in progress · 0 not started</sub>

| | Surface | Kind | VMS | Status | Auth | Scope | Evidence / notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 🟡 | `cs$arg-passing` | feature | Argument list: by reference / value / descriptor | partial | real | in | `src/libvms/include/descrip.h` — Works for C via the native host ABI; VMS's own item-list/arg-block conventions honored for descriptor args. Real, not verified — no cross-language oracle is gated. |
| 🟡 | `cs$data-types` | feature | Standard data types passed across the call boundary | partial | real | in | `src/libvms/include/descrip.h` — Descriptor classes S/D real and marshalled. descrip.h now DECLARES the full class enum (A/NCA/VS/VSA/SD/UBS/...) and dtype set, but no RTL operates on classes A (array) or VS (varying string) and packed decimal is unmarshalled (OTS$ CVT_T_P/CVT_P_T absent); VAX F/D/G/H float unsupported (IEEE only). These declared-but-unmarshalled types are what block Fortran/COBOL/BASIC cross-calls. |
| 🟡≈ | `cs$condition-handling` | feature | Condition-handling as part of the standard (handler search, unwind) | partial | advisory | in | `src/libvms/rtl/lib_signal.c` — In-process handler stack, not a real machine-frame unwind; SYS$UNWIND simplified. Cross-ref chf facility. Advisory: tracked honestly, not a faked full unwind. |
| 🟡≈ | `cs$register-usage` | feature | Register/stack usage conventions (VAX/Alpha/I64 calling standard) | partial | advisory | in | OVMX uses the host (x86_64/aarch64 SysV) ABI, honestly — not the VAX/Alpha VMS register convention; fine for recompiled C, wrong for binary/MACRO interop. Advisory, not a facade. |

### compilers — Compilers (language front-ends)
<sub>scope: undecided · plan: vms-082 · ref: VSI OpenVMS language reference manuals (Fortran/COBOL/BASIC/Pascal/MACRO/…) · reviewed 2026-09-14</sub>

VMS ships a large family of DEC/VSI compilers. OVMX has exactly one language — C, via tcc (the self-hosting beachhead; 549 files under third-party/tcc on origin/main). Every other VMS language is absent — grep on origin/main finds no FOR$/COB$/BAS$/PAS$ RTL and no MACRO-32 front-end. Which of them are in 1.0 scope is an operator call (vms-082); the "run corpus software" goal (R2) leans on Fortran/COBOL/BASIC, so this is not automatically out-of-scope. Absent languages fail at compile time — the correct failure mode, never a facade.

### language-rtl — Language-specific run-time libraries (FOR$/COB$/BAS$/PAS$)
<sub>scope: undecided · plan: vms-082 · ref: VSI OpenVMS language RTL references · reviewed 2026-09-14</sub>

Each VMS language ships a run-time library its compiled code links against (I/O, intrinsics, string/array support). None of the language-specific RTLs exist in OVMX — grep on origin/main for FOR$/COB$/BAS$/PAS$/PLI$ across src/** returns 0 files. The language-INDEPENDENT RTLs they build on (LIB$/STR$/MTH$/ OTS$) are catalogued in domain A and are the shared floor these would sit on — itself only partial, and short exactly the pieces the language RTLs need.
